extracted.intended_audience: Biomedical researchers (prospective HHMI Investigator applicants) and host-institution research leaders
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the qualities, expectations, and program features HHMI uses to select and support Investigators (the Institute's long-term, flexible funding appointments) and the criteria for HHMI Collaborative Innovation Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection philosophy — 'people, not projects'
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI's philosophy of selecting “people, not projects” seeks researchers who bring innovative approaches to the study of many different biological problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI prioritizes the investigator's creativity, trajectory, and ability to pursue important problems over a fixed, narrow project proposal. The emphasis is on the person’s potential to make long-term contributions rather than on a single predefined project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are described as 'widely known for their creativity and productivity' and are expected to be 'pushing the bounds of knowledge in biomedical research.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate a track record of creative ideas and productive research output that indicate capacity to advance their field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to take risks and explore unproven avenues
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI urges its researchers to take risks, explore unproven avenues, and embrace the unknown—even if it means uncertainty or the chance of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors candidates willing to pursue high-risk, high-reward directions. Proposals or career narratives that emphasize conservative or incremental approaches are less aligned with HHMI's stated values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue significant biological questions with rigor and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators 'identify and pursue significant biological questions in a rigorous and deep manner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation looks for investigators who frame important, substantive questions and demonstrate methodological rigor and depth in addressing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new tools and methods; enable creative experimental approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators 'develop new tools and methods that enable creative experimental approaches to biological questions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show evidence of methodological or technological innovation (new tools, techniques, or approaches) that enable novel experiments or lines of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary use of concepts or techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary investigators bring to bear concepts or techniques from other disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-disciplinary fluency and the ability to integrate methods or concepts from adjacent fields (e.g., biophysics, chemical biology, engineering, computational biology) are valued. Evidence of successful interdisciplinary work strengthens an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forge links between basic biology and medicine (translational potential)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators 'forge links between basic biology and medicine, opening new pathways for disease diagnosis and drug discovery.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that creates clear pathways to medical impact or translational applications is specifically highlighted as a desirable outcome of HHMI-supported research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth across biomedical and adjacent disciplines (eligible fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHMI seeks researchers across biomedical disciplines (genetics, cell biology, developmental biology, biochemistry, neuroscience) and adjacent fields (biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, computational biology); plant scientists, evolutionary biologists, and patient-oriented researchers are also included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants from a wide range of basic and adjacent biological fields are eligible and encouraged; selection is not limited to a narrow list of specialties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support bold research in underfunded areas (example: plant science)
rubrics_metrics.description: Through a partnership with the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, HHMI supports creative plant biologists to pursue bold research that could result in large contributions to science and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI explicitly targets underfunded but high-potential areas (e.g., plant biology) and values 'bold' projects with potential for large impact on science and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term, flexible support and expectation to follow ideas to fruition
rubrics_metrics.description: By employing scientists as investigators rather than awarding grants for specific projects, HHMI provides long-term, flexible funding that gives researchers the freedom to explore and, if necessary, change direction. Investigators have support to follow their ideas through to fruition, even if that process takes a very long time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should convey the candidate’s ability to use flexible support productively over long time horizons; HHMI favors researchers who can take advantage of non-project-restricted funding to pursue evolving, long-term research agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with host institution (educational and administrative participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators continue to participate in educational and administrative activities at their host institutions while being supported by HHMI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHMI expects investigators to remain integrated with their host institutions—contributing to teaching, mentoring, and institution-level responsibilities—while receiving HHMI support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment term and renewal standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment is for a five-year term, which may be renewed after an exacting review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial selection is for five years; continued HHMI support requires passing a rigorous renewal review, implying sustained performance and continued alignment with HHMI expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHMI Collaborative Innovation Awards (HCIA) — interdisciplinary, transformative, team-based projects
rubrics_metrics.description: HCIA support interdisciplinary teams of scientists, each headed by an HHMI investigator, to pursue potentially transformative research projects that are new and so large in scope that they require a team with a range of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates for HCIA should propose projects that are interdisciplinary, novel, potentially transformative, and of sufficient scale to justify a multi-investigator team. Collaborators receive funds for up to four years and are expected to use the flexibility to pursue ambitious collaborative work.
